title: The reflection: what it reads, what it may adapt, and what never
note: The reflection factory (2026-09-29, P4 of docs/comportement-en-donnees.fr.md) proposes an adaptation of the conduct from the patterns the station reads in a fork's traces (lib/reflection.ts, observe). An adaptation is a patch on one file of `adaptable`, never on one of `never`, which holds what learning may not adapt even in a fork: the library and its signatures, the facts and the guard's rules, who decides, and the reflection's own bounds (this file). Applied, the file must still be what its reader needs (`consumers` for the playbooks; every key and hole for the words). The station adopts it in a fork only.

never.why: what a factory is told is what a person wrote; what it learns goes to its memory (specs/harness/memory.json), never into its instructions
the library and its signatures are what a person reviewed and signed
a fact is a person's reading of a source, signed
the guard's rules judge the conduct; the conduct does not rewrite its judge
who may decide (the roles) is not the learner's to change
the reflection's own bounds and conduct: a learner that widens its own freedom is no longer measured
the evaluator's factory: what reads the factories' failures is not adapted by what it reads
what the core knows of the application
the memory is written by the station's consolidation, from the evidence of the episodes, never by a patch
